beats.note: At its most basic level, encryption is the process of transforming readable information into an unreadable format so that unauthorized people cannot understand it.
The original readable information is called plaintext.
Encryption uses a mathematical algorithm and a key to transform the plaintext into ciphertext.
Ciphertext may look like a random sequence of letters, numbers, or symbols.
Although the ciphertext still contains the original information, it is designed to be meaningless to anyone who does not have the correct key.
